items.text: The reaction looks exactly the same. The only difference is that this time a solution of magnesium chloride is formed.

items.label: section_header
items.text: EXTENSION WORK

items.label: text
items.text: Acids in solution form ions. Dilute sulfuric acid contains hydrogen ions and sulfate ions. Dilute hydrochloric acid contains hydrogen ions and chloride ions.

items.label: text
items.text: You can rewrite the equations above as ionic equations. In the case of sulfuric acid:

items.label: formula
items.text: M g ( s ) + 2 H ^ { + } ( a q ) + \left ( S O _ { 4 } ^ { 2 - } ( a q ) + M g ^ { 2 * } ( a q ) + \left ( S O _ { 4 } ^ { 2 - } ( a q ) + H _ { 2 } ( g ) \right ) \right )

items.label: text
items.text: The sulfate ion hasn't been changed by the reaction. It is a spectator ion, and so we don't include it in the ionic equation:

items.label: formula
items.text: M g ( s ) + 2 H ^ { + } ( a q ) \rightarrow M g ^ { 2 + } ( a q ) + H _ { 2 } ( g )

items.label: text
items.text: Repeating this with hydrochloric acid, we find that the chloride ions are also spectator ions:

items.label: formula
items.text: M g ( s ) + 2 H ^ { + } ( a q ) + \left ( 2 C I ^ { - } ( a q ) \rightarrow M g ^ { 2 } ( a q ) + \left ( 2 C I ^ { - } ( a q ) + H _ { 2 } ( g ) \right )

items.label: text
items.text: Not including the spectator ions produces the ionic equation:

items.label: text
items.text: The reactions look the same because they are the same. All solutions of acids contain hydrogen ions. That means that magnesium will react with any simple dilute acid in the same way.

items.label: section_header
items.text: REACTIONS INVOLVING ZINC AND ACIDS

items.label: text
items.text: Again, the reactions between zinc and the two acids look exactly the same. The reactions are slower because zinc is lower down the reactivity series than magnesium.

items.label: text
items.text: The equations are:

items.label: formula
items.text: Z n ( s ) + H _ { 2 } S O _ { 4 } ( a q ) & \to Z n S O _ { 4 } ( a q ) + H _ { 2 } ( g ) \\ Z n ( s ) + 2 H C l ( a q ) & \to Z n C l _ { 2 } ( a q ) + H _ { 2 } ( g )
